description:
About the Position

Utrecht University invites applications for a PhD position within the CUE-CAN project on the environmental causes of childhood and early-onset cancer. The project studies how environmental exposures early in life relate to the risk of childhood and early-onset cancers, using large-scale registries, geospatial exposure data and modern epidemiological methods.

The doctoral candidate will design and run analyses linking population registries with environmental exposure models, contribute to study protocols and data infrastructure, and publish on exposure-outcome associations. The position sits within the university's strong epidemiology environment and is a salaried four-year track under the CAO-NU collective agreement.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in epidemiology, public health, biomedical sciences, environmental science or a related quantitative discipline. Skills in statistical programming and register-based research are important; affinity with environmental health questions is essential. The working language is English, and the supervisory team spans paediatric oncology epidemiology and environmental health.

Highlights

  • Environmental exposures and cancer risk
  • Register-based and geospatial epidemiology
  • Exposure modelling and data linkage
  • Childhood and early-onset cancer aetiology
  • Large-scale population data analysis
  • Salaried four-year PhD under the CAO-NU agreement

About Utrecht University

Utrecht University is a leading Dutch research university, consistently ranked among the top institutions in Europe. Its research and teaching span four faculties and a broad range of strategic themes, including sustainability, dynamics of youth, institutions for open societies and life sciences. PhD candidates and postdocs in the Netherlands are salaried staff members with full employment benefits under the CAO-NU collective agreement, so advertised positions are fully funded. Academic and support vacancies are published on the university's working-at portal, with clear deadlines and application instructions per position.
